claims.claim: Added an explicit nondefault Runtime feedback-consumption API bound to the original Dispatcher and ExecutorBoundary invocation. Default dispatch paths retain their existing behavior.
Consumption freshly authenticates exact admission, current candidate, complete reviewed native K_i, original captures and immutable F_i bytes through existing Runtime gates.

Feedback requires the original current registry holder, adapter, profile and executing thread. Immutable invocation intent blocks reconstructed or repeated prospective invocation before native execute.
Only direct same-invocation adapter confirmation creates a local acknowledgment bound to K_i/F_i and protected Runtime/invocation identities; production and continuation authorities remain denied.

Exact replay reconciles original retained receipt bytes without another callback, proof execution, adapter invocation or resource debit. Conflicts and ambiguous effects retain original records and block reentry.

Continuation assessment always returns non-actionable STOP. Progress requires authenticated scoped descendant history and reduced original failures; finite Human opt-in and token/budget authority remain NOT_ESTABLISHED.
Terminal state, competing mutation, revoked source and uncertain sessions block acknowledgment authority. REPAIR and REMEDIATION cannot consume PRIMARY feedback.
Closed bounded codecs expose fixed statuses, factual identities and counters while excluding raw logs, secrets, executable instructions, patches and caller-asserted authority.

Added focused test definitions using real Git/native checkpoint fixtures and actual RunLeaseRegistry/ExecutorBoundary invocation, covering local acknowledgment, replay, identity substitution, source corruption, terminal contention, crash ambiguity, progress and correction spoofing.
Committed changes are confined to the seven permitted paths. Documentation identifies L3-04 as preactivation and keeps L3-05, L3-06/G3, G6 and L4 obligations separate.
